annotation.title_clean: Civil liability regime for artificial intelligence: European Parliament resolution of 20 October 2020 with recommendations to the Commission (2020/2014(INL))
annotation.title_en: Civil liability regime for artificial intelligence: European Parliament resolution of 20 October 2020 with recommendations to the Commission (2020/2014(INL))
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, C 404/107 (6.10.2021)
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament legislative-initiative resolution asking the Commission to propose a Regulation on civil liability for AI-system operators. It proposes strict liability and mandatory insurance for listed high-risk AI systems, fault-based liability with presumed fault for others, compensation caps, and a revised Product Liability Directive. It rejects legal personality for AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: Strict liability for operators of high-risk AI-systems listed in an Annex, updated by delegated acts at least every six months
Fault-based liability with presumption of fault for non-listed AI-systems
Mandatory liability insurance for high-risk AI operators; compensation caps of EUR 2m (death/injury) and EUR 1m (property/immaterial harm)
Frontend and backend operators jointly and severally liable; Product Liability Directive to be revised in parallel
AI-systems need no legal personality; liability falls on persons controlling the risk
